abstract: 党的十八大以来，以习近平同志为核心的党中央对政府和市场关系的规律性认识不断深化，习近平经济思想中关于新型政府和市场关系的重大创新可以概括如下：在制度层面，处理好政府和市场关系，本质上是社会主义与市场经济的有机结合，必须加强党对经济工作的全面领导，以坚持基本经济制度为根基，以构建法治经济为保障；在体制层面，政府和市场关系是对立统一的辩证关系，社会主义市场经济中政府作用超越了仅弥补“市场失灵”的职能，并且处理政府和市场关系要适应改革与开放的互动；在运行层面，处理政府和市场关系要促进效率最优化与效益最大化，兼顾活力与秩序，做到既“放得活”又“管得好”，统筹发展和安全。发挥市场机制在产业之内、产业之间、消费与积累之间的资源配置作用，同时更好发挥政府在建立市场制度、完善宏观经济治理体系、促进各种所有制经济共同发展、扎实推进共同富裕、完善科技创新体制机制、推动可持续发展等方面的作用。中国共产党作为最高政治领导力量，通过谋划全局、推动改革、协调各方、强化落实，统筹政府和市场作用的发挥。“十五五”时期要进一步处理好政府和市场关系，加快构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制。

abstract: 中国在改革开放以来特别是党的十八大以来的宏观经济管理实践中，逐步探索形成了一套有别于西方发达国家传统上以周期为导向的宏观政策的理念和做法，具有鲜明的以发展为导向的特征。本文从学理上将其提炼概括为“发展导向型宏观调控”，并构建了一个四象限分析框架刻画其理论内涵。与西方发达国家传统的单维度、局限于短期、侧重于需求侧的狭义周期导向型宏观政策不同，中国的发展导向型宏观调控具有总量和结构双维度、短期和中长期并重、兼顾供给侧与需求侧的特征。以周期为导向的西方传统宏观政策理论主要基于历史上发达国家的宏观政策实践，与广大发展中国家宏观经济管理的现实需要之间存在“鸿沟”；而发展导向型宏观调控源于中国这一世界上最大的发展中国家的成功实践，兼具促进经济持续增长、推动结构转型升级、化解重点领域供需失衡、平滑总量经济波动等综合职能，内涵更为丰富，包含并超越了狭义的逆周期宏观政策，更加适用于广大发展中国家的现实需要。这一标识性概念的提出，是在宏观经济领域以习近平经济思想为指导构建中国经济学自主知识体系的一种尝试，既是对中国过往宏观经济管理实践的理论总结，也对未来进一步完善宏观调控和健全宏观经济治理体系具有启示意义，同时有望为其他国家尤其是发展中国家的宏观经济管理提供一定参考借鉴。

abstract: 合作创新是打破创新要素市场分割的重要切入点。如何发挥土地要素市场化配置在城市间合作创新中的引导作用，是充分释放城市创新效能的关键议题。本文立足产业结构趋同的新视角，以2007年工业用地市场化配置改革为外生冲击，探讨土地要素市场化配置对城市间合作创新的影响效果与作用机制。研究发现，土地要素市场化配置通过推动城市产业专业化，强化了产业结构趋同的禀赋优势，并依托技术兼容与供应链关联机制，加快城市间知识溢出，促进了城市间合作创新，凸显了产业结构趋同的“合意性”特征。此外，行政壁垒的弱化将促进土地要素市场化配置的合作创新效应，且这一促进作用在同一省份、同一城市群以及相邻城市对中更为明显；而降低交通成本有助于破除创新要素流动的空间壁垒，激发土地要素市场化配置的区域整体创新发展活力。上述结论不仅拓展了产业空间组织与创新地理的理论边界，而且为疏通创新要素流动堵点、推动创新要素市场一体化提供了经验证据与实践参考。

abstract: 智能算力是推动AI创新的关键要素，但较高的算力获取成本可能制约中小企业开展AI创新。本文利用自2019年以来各地先后建设公共人工智能计算中心这一准自然实验，采用多期双重差分模型考察公共智算中心建设对中小企业AI创新的影响。研究发现，公共智算中心建设显著增加了企业的AI专利申请数量，且这一影响在AI企业和潜在算力需求较强的企业中更为明显。公共智算中心建设还促进了企业研发投入和AI技能人才配置。异质性分析表明，公共智算中心建设对民营企业和小规模企业AI创新的促进作用更强。进一步研究发现，公共智算中心建设提高了AI创新质量，促进了AI知识向其他技术领域扩散，并提升了企业全要素生产率。本文从公共算力供给的视角，为理解新型数字基础设施如何促进中小企业AI创新提供了经验证据，也为优化公共算力资源配置、完善普惠算力供给体系提供了政策启示。

abstract: 在数字经济加快发展与碳排放双控约束持续强化的背景下，数字化带来的效率红利能否充分转化为绿色红利，已成为统筹数字经济发展与绿色低碳转型过程中亟待回答的重要问题。本文以国家级大数据综合试验区设立为准自然实验，基于2006—2019年中国城市面板数据，构建三重差分模型，识别大数据政策的碳回弹风险、作用机制及缓释条件。研究发现：第一，国家级大数据综合试验区显著抬升了回弹风险，即政策实施后，相同幅度的碳效率改善所对应的减排幅度有所减小。第二，机制分析表明，传统的能源—劳动替代效应未获经验支持；产出效应主要体现为固定资产投资和政府支出扩张，数字资本与能源投入之间的互补效应进一步强化了数字化扩张的能源需求，构成更具数字经济特征的碳回弹渠道。第三，新型能源禀赋和新型电力系统是碳回弹的重要缓释条件。清洁能源供给与电力配置能力越强，新增数字用能越能得到低碳电力体系的有效承接，碳回弹风险越低。本文还提出了有针对性的政策建议，指出应完善数字基础设施绿色绩效评价，强化数字资本全生命周期节能管理，并推动算力布局与新型电力系统协同规划。

abstract: 针对主流宏观经济学“长期—短期二分法”研究范式的视角局限，本文结合实证分析与理论建模，把短期经济波动与中长期增长纳入统一分析框架，系统揭示了中国货币政策与财政政策的中长期效应及其作用机制。首先，本文构建工具变量局部投影模型进行经验分析，证实两类政策对总产出存在中长期效应；其次，基于纳入内生增长机制及基础设施建设、金融市场摩擦、国企民企差异等中国经济特征的动态一般均衡模型，进一步探讨了上述效应的产生机制。本文发现：（1）扩张性货币政策与政府公共投资扩张均能提高长期总产出，而政府消费扩张则相反；（2）不同类型政策长期效应的差异在于其对企业研发的影响不同；（3）金融摩擦通过扭曲实物资本投资与研发投入的相对收益抑制企业研发，而适度的公共资本可发挥纠偏作用；（4）降低整体金融摩擦或缩小企业间融资差异能够显著提升政策效能。据此，本文提出了优化中国宏观调控体系的政策建议。

abstract: 本文从服务型政府视角为建设全国统一大市场提供新的理论解释和量化证据。在理论层面，本文构建了一个包含政务服务市场的一般均衡模型，证明统一服务型政府行为促进全国统一大市场建设的理论机制是效率提升效应和要素流动效应。前者提升全要素生产率，是长期效应；后者促进生产要素流动，是短期效应。在实证层面，本文采用73个代表性城市数据，聚焦“高效办成一件事”改革，量化分析这两个效应的水平，结果发现，在2018—2024年间，两个效应在代表性城市普遍存在，并且带动了代表性城市的经济增长。本文还量化分析了全国统一服务型政府行为的长期效应，结果显示，统一服务型政府行为还可促进全国经济长期增长水平进一步提升。这些量化结果与理论预期一致，有助于系统性理解统一服务型政府行为对建设全国统一大市场和促进经济高质量发展的重要意义。

abstract: 强大的货币是建设金融强国的关键核心金融要素之一。近年来，人民币国际化取得了一定进展，人民币在国际贸易融资货币中的占比有所上升，但人民币计价安全资产（如人民币国债）的规模和国际持有量仍然非常有限。本文围绕“国债市场推动人民币国际化的内在机制和政策路径”这一核心问题，基于贸易融资与安全资产互动的视角构建了一个多国动态一般均衡模型，刻画了企业在贸易融资中的安全资产及货币选择机制，通过多重均衡框架下的区制转移分析，识别了国际货币体系从美元主导均衡向多极化均衡演进的边界条件，展现了美元主导地位下降、人民币国际地位上升的动态路径，量化分析了提高国债市场交易效率、扩大国债市场规模、提升国债市场开放程度等不同政策工具对人民币国际化的独立边际效应和条件边际效应。研究发现，在三种政策工具同时发挥作用的情形下，不同政策对人民币国际化的条件边际效应存在明显差异：当人民币国债市场交易效率提升至与美国国债市场相当的水平时，人民币国际化程度显著提高，且提升幅度最大；当人民币国债市场规模扩大至与美国国债市场相当的量级时，人民币国际化程度同样明显提升，其促进作用仅次于交易效率改善；当人民币国债市场逐步实现完全开放时，人民币国际化水平会得到一定程度的提高，但边际效应不及前二者。研究结果揭示了国债市场高质量发展与高水平开放对人民币国际化的关键作用，验证了以国债市场推动人民币国际化的政策有效性。

abstract: 在扩大内需和消费升级转型背景下，如何通过财政政策提振消费并优化消费结构，已成为重要宏观经济问题。区别于主要从总消费层面评估财政政策效应的研究，本文构建包含收入不确定性的异质性个体生命周期多部门消费模型，将居民消费划分为非耐用品消费、耐用品消费和服务消费三类，并利用中国家庭金融调查（CHFS）数据进行结构估计；在此基础上，以2018年个人所得税改革为基准政策冲击，评估其对居民消费及消费结构的影响，并通过反事实模拟比较不同政策工具作用。研究发现，改革提高了居民消费水平，并推动消费支出由非耐用品消费向耐用品消费和服务消费转移，该效应由减税规模与家庭边际消费倾向异质性共同决定。进一步分析表明，继续提高起征点的边际作用有限，而低收入群体税额返还和服务消费补贴在扩大消费和促进消费结构升级方面更为有效。从分配效应与政策效率看，低收入群体税额返还和服务消费补贴表现更优。此外，改善收入预期、降低收入不确定性也有助于提振消费并优化消费结构。本文分析表明，扩大内需不仅取决于消费总量增长，也取决于政策设计能否在稳定收入预期的同时兼顾消费扩张、结构优化与分配改善。

abstract: 我国居民医保参保率已经较高，但存在参保动员成本高、催缴难的问题，需要提升参保的内在激励，并促进医保基金运行的可持续性。本文基于我国居民医保参保中的不一致选择行为，论证参保激励措施的效果。文章检验了不一致选择的存在，即同样的现金支出，保费比预期自付医疗费用对人们参保选择的影响更大。健康较好的低风险人群的不一致选择更普遍，且该群体的不一致选择降低了参保中的逆选择。收入较低群体的不一致选择主要受收入约束。政府动员增强了低风险人群的不一致选择，但减弱了低收入群体的不一致选择。模拟表明，在完全理性选择下，对低风险人群降低保费比提高医保待遇更能促进其参保，更有利于医保基金收支平衡。此外，按照家庭人均可支配收入确定保费对整体参保率提升有限，高收入群体参保率有所下降，但能显著减轻低收入群体的缴费负担，提升其参保积极性。本文的发现为加强居民医保参保激励、实现可持续的全民医保提供了参考。

abstract: 机器替代人的生产方式变革，冲击着以稳定劳动关系和劳动收入报酬作为社保缴费基础的传统社保筹资机制，削弱社会保障的可持续性。本文利用全国税收调查数据匹配工业机器人渗透度，系统考察了机器人使用对企业社会保险缴费的影响及其作用机制，并讨论了增强社会保险基金可持续性的可能路径。研究表明，机器人使用会通过劳动替代效应缩减企业劳动雇佣规模和缴费基础，同时也会通过工资收入效应提高企业社会保险缴费，但就业替代效应占主导地位，最终表现出对企业社保缴费的负向作用。进一步研究发现，机器人使用会通过就业再配置效应，推动劳动力流向服务业和非正规就业部门，但由于服务业部门社会保险缴费规范性较低、灵活就业群体社会保险缴费连续性较弱，新增就业并未同步形成稳定的社会保险缴费增量，最终总体上仍表现为参保人数和社保基金收入下降。为增强社保可持续性，在短期内应提高缴费规范性，增强财政支持力度；长期来看，仍需优化社会保险筹资模式，构建与生产技术变革相适应的社会保障体制和管理机制。

abstract: This paper presents a detailed economic modelling analysis of public finance in the transition towards carbon neutrality. We outline results from a Net-Zero Emission Ambition scenario, reflecting the ambition to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions globally by mid-century, using a broad and region-specific policy package that combines various policy instruments: carbon pricing, removal of fossil fuel support, regulations in the power sector, and other policies that stimulate investments by firms and households to reduce and decarbonise energy use. The analysis relies on the OECD global computable general equilibrium ENV-Linkages model. Our results show that transitioning towards emissions neutrality involves relatively modest economic and fiscal consequences. The scenario achieves emissions neutrality while maintaining continued economic growth, despite a limited negative impact on global GDP (which excludes the benefits from reduced climate damages) and on public revenues. In our central scenario we find that net public revenues slightly decrease globally in 2050 (−0.5% of Baseline GDP). The fiscal effects reflect a trade-off between instruments that increase public revenues (carbon pricing) or reduce public expenditures (fossil fuel subsidies removal), on the one hand, and more costly instruments (subsidies) and indirect effects (tax base erosion and changes in fiscal and economic structure) on the other hand.
title: Public finance resilience in the transition towards carbon neutrality: a computable general equilibrium analysis

abstract: This paper examines how prosocial motivations shape lying behavior in a strategic setting. Two players each privately choose a color in their mind, then draw a color at random, and report whether the two colors match. Both players receive a high payoff if at least one reports a match, so a single lie secures the payoff for both, making lies strategic substitutes. I develop a theoretical model in which individuals bear a psychological cost of lying but experience a lower cost when their lie increases their partner’s payoff. The model predicts that individuals are less likely to lie when they can rely on their partner to do so, and more likely to lie when their dishonesty benefits their partner. I test these predictions in an online experiment with four treatments that separately vary the opportunity to rely on the partner’s lie and the presence of a benefit to the partner. In this setting, prosocial motives outweigh lying aversion: participants lie more when their dishonesty benefits their partner, and they do not lie less when they can leave the lie to their partner. Lying increases only when a participant’s report is pivotal to the partner’s payoff, indicating that prosocial preferences reduce the net cost of lying when dishonesty is instrumental in generating benefits for others.
title: The impact of lying aversion and prosocial lies on cheating

abstract: An individual reports subjective beliefs over continuous events using a proper scoring rule, such as the Quadratic Scoring Rule. Under mild additional assumptions, it is known that these reports reflect latent subjective beliefs if the individual is risk neutral. We demonstrate how to fully recover latent subjective beliefs if the individual is known to distort probabilities into decision weights using Rank Dependent Utility theory, and generalize all results for the complete class of proper scoring rules. As an immediate corollary, we can then exactly recover latent subjective beliefs using Expected Utility Theory. Using Bayesian econometric methods, we demonstrate how to recover belief distributions for individuals, and illustrate these results by recovering belief distributions about the “competitiveness” of individuals and the addictiveness of smoking. These results significantly widen the domain of applicability of proper scoring rules for eliciting latent subjective belief distributions.
title: Recovering subjective probability distributions: a Bayesian approach

abstract: We develop a real options framework for the optimal timing of climate policy when both economic cost and stocks of environmental pollutants evolve stochastically and are correlated. By modelling environmental damage as a mean-reverting pollution stock jointly driven with uncertain economic losses, we extend the single-uncertainty specifications of Pindyck (2000) and the uncorrelated two-dimensional specification of Pindyck (2002). The resulting policy-adoption problem is formulated as a two-dimensional variational inequality (VI). We derive the post-policy value function in closed form and obtain an analytical necessary-condition curve that provides a sub-optimal stopping rule. Consistent with the correction of the proposed closed-form pre-policy stopping solutions by Balikcioglu et al. (2011), we compute the pre-policy value function and the globally optimal boundary numerically from the contact set of the VI. Across the configurations considered, the optimal stopping boundary is decreasing and predominantly convex in the pollution stock. The effect of uncertainty on policy timing is not uniform. In the main sensitivity exercise, positive correlation causes greater pollution-stock volatility to lower the boundary and accelerate adoption, whereas greater economic-cost volatility raises the boundary, with a smaller additional increase at higher volatility levels. Under negative correlation, greater volatility in either state variable raises the boundary and delays adoption. Under the nested single-uncertainty and uncorrelated zero-decay benchmark specifications (Pindyck, 2000; 2002), our numerical solutions produce the conventional uncertainty-delay ordering, qualitatively consistent with the corrected numerical boundaries reported by Balikcioglu et al. (2011 ). In a positively correlated extension of the uncorrelated two-dimensional benchmark, however, greater economic-cost volatility lowers the boundary. Policy timing therefore depends on the full joint-risk specification and the broader parameter configuration, rather than on volatility or correlation considered alone.
journal: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
title: On the Role of Uncertainty in Timing Environmental Policies

abstract: Rules are central to social order, but violations can rapidly spread when compliance is costly to individuals. Here we study rule-following under situational ambiguity, where the applicability of rules is open to interpretation. It is currently unclear how such ambiguity shapes rule compliance and the sway of social influence. We present incentivized experiments (total n = 3226 American Prolific workers) showing that situational ambiguity substantially reduces rule compliance. Observing rule bending or a rule violation reduces compliance, whereas observing compliance does not increase it. The combined effect of situational ambiguity and observing a rule violation is as strong as the effect of either factor on its own, suggesting that many people comply unless an opportunity arises for rule violations that increase their monetary payoffs. Further experiments suggest that these results are partly driven by weakened social norms: situational ambiguity reduces disapproval of rule bending, and observing non-compliance increases expectations that others will violate the rule.
title: Situational ambiguity induces opportunistic rule breaking and erodes social norms

abstract: An investment boom can coexist with investor skepticism about the claims supporting individual projects. We study investors who can identify an interested insider behind a public report before exercising a risky investment option. Verification improves the investor’s decision and deters manipulation by reducing the capital attracted by a false favorable report. Verification informs privately but disciplines publicly. Investors capture the first benefit but ignore the second, so the market verifies too little. Manipulation raises the private value of verification, making verification choices strategic substitutes and equilibrium unique. With intermediate common costs, scrutiny vanishes and manipulated reports direct capital to bad projects under Bayesian beliefs. Rational skepticism can sustain collective misinvestment when credibility is a public good.
title: Skepticism without scrutiny: Verification and information manipulation

abstract: We study the incentives properties of one of the central solutions to the problem of allocating divisible commodities among equally entitled agents, namely the Egalitarian Walrasian rule (EW), when agents have linear preferences. The EW rule being manipulable on this domain, we ask whether it is, at least, immune to obvious manipulations, in the sense of Troyan and Morrill (2020). Unfortunately, the answer is negative. This manipulability result is generic since we show that any agent for whom all the commodities are desirable has an obvious manipulation.
title: The genericity of obvious manipulations under the Egalitarian Walrasian rule when preferences are linear

abstract: Land use and land cover (LULC) change strongly affects hydrology, irrigation performance, and agricultural sustainability in tropical basins. However, despite the availability of historical LULC mapping, spatially explicit projections of future land use dynamics for the Bogowonto Watershed remain limited, particularly for supporting long-term spatial planning and irrigation management. This study applied a hybrid Cellular Automata-Artificial Neural Network (CA-ANN) model with the MOLUSCE plugin in QGIS to analyze LULC dynamics in the Bogowonto Watershed, Central Java, Indonesia. Random Forest classification of Landsat imagery (2015-2023) achieved accuracies above 89% and Kappa values of 0.86–0.93. Historical analysis revealed a 76.1% increase during the 2015–2023 period in built-up areas (3,136.28ha in 2015 to 5,523.56ha in 2023). This growth was accompanied by a 5.2% decline in high-density vegetation and a gradual conversion of rice fields, primarily into built-up areas. Projections to 2103 suggest that built-up areas nearly double or 89.93% compared to the 2023 baseline, while rice fields may shrink by 44%, posing risks for food security, irrigation infrastructure, and agricultural sustainability. An overlay with the 2044 Regional Spatial Plan indicates spatial consistency, as much of the projected urban growth occurs within designated settlement and industrial zones. Yet, the projected extent of conversion exceeds the planned capacity of these zones, underscoring the urgent need for adaptive planning that integrates spatial LULC projections into irrigation and agricultural policies.
title: Predicting Future Land Use and Land Cover Dynamics in a Tropical Watershed for Irrigation Planning and Agricultural Sustainability Using a Hybrid Modelling Approach

abstract: The expansion of protected areas (PAs) is a crucial tool to halt biodiversity loss, promote conservation of ecosystems, and protect valuable parts of the landscape. The United Nations (UN) has adopted the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and the European Union (EU) has its own EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030; both documents aim to protect 30% of the land and sea. The State Programme of Nature Conservation and Landscape Protection of the Czech Republic states that the network of PAs has not been finalized yet. We gathered data on ecosystem and landscape quality (biodiversity, natural and cultural values, and anthropogenic transformation) to make a comprehensive prioritization analysis to find out where national parks (NP) and protected landscape areas (PLA) could be designated and extended in Czechia. Based on Zonation analysis, current NPs are naturally the most valuable parts of Czechia. However, there are still many areas of high importance that are not protected and where protection at the level of NP or PLA should be introduced. Overall, our prioritization suggests that about 20% of the country should be protected as PLAs and 6% as NPs. We identify 36 candidate PLAs, 21 candidate NPs and 31 candidate extensions of existing large PAs. Many of them have been discussed for decades; some of them are in the process of designation. Due to biodiversity loss and landscape quality deterioration, urgent action to protect the most valuable sites is needed. The presented methodology provides a systematic and data-driven tool for delineating priority areas.
title: Priorities and potential for enlarging Czech large-scale protected areas

abstract: Emerging markets are vulnerable to sudden shifts in investor sentiment, which can lead to pressure on exchange rates and financing conditions. Using panel evidence from 23 emerging markets, this column shows that the sensitivity of portfolio flows to global shocks has weakened since the Global Crisis. However, sensitivity varies widely across countries. Countries with more independent central banks and lower levels of public debt experience lower portfolio outflows during periods of global financial stress. The results highlight that although emerging markets cannot control global factors, they can influence their resilience to these shocks.
title: Building resilience to global financial shocks in emerging markets

abstract: When a job vacancy opens, the manager faces a choice: to hire from outside the organisation, or to fill the position with an existing employee through a promotion or horizontal move. This column uses data from Finland to show that more productive firms are more likely to hire from within. As technological change reshapes jobs and the skills they require, the ability to recognise and redeploy existing talent may become increasingly valuable. The most productive firms may have an advantage not only because they have better workers or better technology, but because they are better at seeing the capabilities already inside their organisations.
authors: Ricardo Alonso, Jed DeVaro, Antti Kauhanen, Nelli Valmari
title: Productive firms can better spot and deploy their internal talent

abstract: Betting exchanges match people to take opposite sides of a bet. We present a model of a betting exchange in which participants disagree about outcome probabilities but are, on average, correct. Traders maximize subjective expected profits and equilibrium emerges from a simple matching process. The model predicts those who post quotes (Makers) will earn higher returns than those who accept them (Takers) and that loss rates for Takers will rise as the probability of their accepted bet winning falls. Using a large sample of bets on soccer from Betfair Exchange, we implement a transaction-level empirical strategy that identifies Maker and Taker sides of each trade. We show that pre-match and early in-play behavior aligns closely with the model’s predictions. However, as matches progress, behavior shifts: longshot bets generate large, systematic losses even for liquidity providers, and profits emerge for those who accept offers on favorites
title: Agreeing to Disagree: The Economics of Betting Exchanges

abstract: We study the importance of insurance provided by cash-rich parents to cash-constrained children experiencing earnings shocks. Using matched population data for Norway spanning two generations, we establish several results. First, parents respond to negative labor income shocks faced by their adult children by changing their saving choices. Consistent with dynastic insurance, we observe a negligible response when children’s income shocks are positive. Second, parents’ responses depend on the nature of the shock. Temporary income losses lead parents to dissave, consistent with immediate transfers; persistent losses induce parents to increase savings in anticipation of future transfers. We find that parental insurance is substantial: on average, parents dissave 35 cents of liquid wealth in response to a $1 temporary loss, and set aside an additional 19 cents to fund future transfers in response to a $1 persistent loss. Third, insurance provision is weaker when children have access to alternative smoothing mechanisms, such as spousal labor supply, and it is stronger if children live geographically far from their parents. Finally, we do not find evidence of reverse insurance (children insuring their parents’ labor income losses). Our results have implications for models studying the aggregate consequences of idiosyncratic labor income shocks.
title: Insuring Labor Income Shocks: The Role of the Dynasty

abstract: Starting in 2021, Kalshi was the first federally licensed prediction market in the United States and remains the dominant platform in this segment. Using transaction-level data on over 300,000 contracts, we provide the first systematic evidence on its pricing. Contract prices are informative and become more accurate as markets approach closing, but they display a clear favorite–longshot bias: low-price contracts win far less often than required to break even after fees, while high-price contracts win more often and yield small positive returns. All trades are offered by Makers and accepted by Takers. Makers earn higher returns than Takers, but returns for both exhibit a favorite–longshot pattern. We interpret these facts using a framework that reflects Kalshi’s quote-driven microstructure, in which agents sort into trading decisions based on their beliefs. We find that modest levels of disagreement and a small tendency to overstate small probabilities are sufficient to reproduce the favorite–longshot patterns in the data.
title: Makers and Takers: The Economics of the Kalshi Prediction Market

abstract: We develop a general equilibrium model where workers of different skill groups sort into occupations by comparative advantage. Wages and employment depend on workers’ skill quality, occupation-specific country-embedded productivity, and occupational distortions. Using harmonized microdata for 50 countries, we infer these components from the model’s equilibrium conditions. Workers in rich countries exhibit higher skill quality and substantially greater productivity, especially in white-collar occupations. Human capital explains 52 percent of output-per-worker gaps, largely through the complementarity between skill composition and quality, and further amplified by technology choices biased toward skilled labor. Adopting the U.S. distribution of skill groups yields limited gains for poor countries without higher quality. Occupational distortions are more severe in low-income countries, reducing white-collar employment and raising wage premia, but with modest aggregate effects.
title: From Skills to Occupations: Comparative Advantage and Cross-Country Income Differences

abstract: We study how shifting intra-household control over resources affects fertility, exploiting a quasi-natural experiment in Israel where some Holocaust survivors began receiving substantial, permanent and unexpected reparations in 1957 and others only decades later, after their childbearing years. Using a triple-difference design with heterogeneity by the wife's age, we compare fertility outcomes by timing of reparations, recipient's gender, and age. Households in which the wife was age 25 or younger in 1957 and received reparations early had 0.25--0.4 fewer children than the corresponding male-recipient comparison, after netting out gender differences among late-recipient households. An event study tracking households across the full reproductive span shows that the gap emerged only after 1957 and stabilized at roughly this magnitude by the late 1960s. A complementary within-early-cohort design compares female-only-early to dual-early households among young wives, ruling out selection into early female receipt. The estimate is similar, indicating that the operative margin is the relative shift in spousal control rather than the wife's receipt per se. Suggestive evidence shows higher educational attainment among the affected children, consistent with a quantity--quality reallocation. The findings speak to the design of individually paid unconditional transfers and child-contingent pronatalist policies.
title: She who Pays the Piper Calls the Number: Reparations and Gender Differences in Fertility Choice

abstract: We review the ``production approach'' to estimating markups, the ratio of price to marginal cost. The approach is scalable. It requires no model of consumer demand or market structure and applies broadly across firms, industries, and time. We organize our review around a simple insight: the production-based markup is a residual. Like the Solow residual, it is clean in theory but potentially contaminated by misspecification and mismeasurement. This framing helps explain why small differences in implementation can produce starkly different results from the same data. In some cases, estimated markups have risen sharply. In others, they have not. We provide conceptual rationales for these disagreements, offer practical guidance on data and estimation, and call for greater transparency about how much of the variation attributed to markups may instead reflect technology.
title: Micro and Macro Perspectives on Production-Based Markups

abstract: Over one billion people in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) work in food systems, including informal actors such as traditional, street, and mobile vendors, who contribute to food environments critical for food and nutrition security. Despite their role in LMIC food environments, research on how informality is defined and its influence remains limited, creating significant policy gaps. This systematic review addresses these gaps by examining how informality in food environments is defined and empirically studied, and how it intersects with nutrition within livelihood and sociopolitical contexts. A search was conducted across fourteen databases on studies published in English after 2000. From 23,250 records, 327 studies across 64 countries were included. Most research (84%) was conducted in urban settings and employed a diverse range of methodologies. Fewer than 25% of articles explicitly defined informality, as compared to the three components of informality defined by the International Labor Organization: 83% of studies defined informality as goods produced for markets, 23% referred to private enterprises, and only 10% mentioned social protection for vendors. Common food products studied included prepared foods, beverages, and vegetables. Key sociopolitical factors influencing informality were regulation, governance, gender dynamics, and access to water, sanitation, and public spaces. Main livelihood challenges included business operations, vendor interactions, and working hours. Results demonstrate that informal food environments are a linchpin for food security and livelihoods in LMICs. Without understanding informal food environment actors from an interdisciplinary and multidimensional perspective, policies will continue to miss these important food system actors.
title: Informality in food environments: a systematic review of nutrition, livelihood, and sociopolitical outcomes and implications for food policy

abstract: Several training programs worldwide are residential, bringing enrollees to live in facilities and thus increasing program costs. In the U.S., the Job Corps (JC) program for disadvantaged youth includes a residential component. Despite extensive literature evaluating JC, the impact of the residential component has received limited attention. We develop and employ a semiparametric model to estimate the average causal effects of this residential component, accounting for selection into both the program and the residential feature. Our findings indicate that, among JC enrollees, the residential component boosts earnings and educational-degree attainment among adolescents. For other subgroups, the residential component has minimal impact on labor market outcomes, with the notable exception of reduced earnings among young adults; it also increases substance use among some subgroups. For example, the average treatment effect of the residential component raises hard drug use by 183 percent among young adults and by 122 percent among females without children. Negative peer effects may explain the increase in detrimental health behaviors.
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization

title: The heterogeneous impacts of the residential component of a training program: A semiparametric analysis

abstract: We study how political regimes affect the dispersion of attitudes within societies. We develop a framework in which authoritarian regimes, through stronger social control and norm enforcement, compress heterogeneity in beliefs, whereas democratic regimes allow greater diversity. Using cross-country survey data, we find positive associations between democracy and attitudinal dispersion across several domains. To provide more diagnostic evidence, we examine differences between former East and West German residents immediately after reunification. Former East German residents exhibit lower attitudinal dispersion in domains plausibly subject to social control, with no comparable difference for private preferences. These findings highlight the role of political regimes in shaping the distribution of beliefs through behavioral channels such as conformity pressures and socialization.
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization

title: Social Control and the Dispersion of Beliefs: Evidence from Cross-Country Data and German Reunification
